title: First Riley-native training campaign — data-centric A/B
objective: Answer with scientific confidence: does Riley's manufactured corpus (realism engineering ON) produce a measurably better guitar separator than a naive corpus built from the EXACT same source material (realism OFF)?
hypothesis: Riley Corpus v1.0 (scenario/masking/DSP realism) will train a separator with higher benchmark + blind-listening quality than the naive flat-mixed baseline, because realistic masking/dynamics/backing balance produce supervision closer to real mixtures.

A_riley.mixing: Riley Virtual Studio — 12 realistic scenarios, per-role masking/level/pan, soft-comp, exact ground truth

B_naive.mixing: naive flat sum — 12 role-set scenarios, masking_db=0, compression=0, no is_masker; SAME guitars + SAME backing pool

arms.note: both arms capped to identical sample count (min of the two, deterministic selection) so dataset SIZE cannot influence the result. Mixing realism is the ONLY variable.

architecture.no_experiments: no architecture/optimizer/loss/hyperparameter exploration — architecture is fixed, the dataset is the experiment

recipe.augmentations: enabled (loudness, mixup, channel_shuffle, polarity) — identical both arms
recipe.adaptation: chunk_size/segment reduced 11s->6s to match the frozen 6s corpus segment; applied IDENTICALLY to both arms (data-fit necessity, not tuning). Everything else unchanged.

evaluation.downstream_gate: frozen sep -> riley_guitar F1 vs GT (T2 gate-eval); training-time validation SDR is silent-reference-contaminated -> descriptive only

promotion_gate.explicitly_not: a two-song win or a narrow single-regime win is NOT a promotion

reproducibility: Model checkpoints tie to arm corpus_hash + this campaign_id + git_sha. Reproducible from the two frozen corpora years from now.
